classification.difficultyReason: Find two heights using the same horizontal distance, then subtract to obtain the flagpole height.

content.prompt:
From a point $P$, 200 m from the base of a building, the angles of elevation of the bottom and top of a flagpole on top of the building are $34^{\circ}$ and $36^{\circ}$ respectively.

Calculate the height, $AB$, of the flagpole. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: An unshaded building at the left supports vertical flagpole AB. Point P is on horizontal ground to the right. Separate nested angle arcs measure elevation from the ground to PA and PB. Decorative windows and the flag are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The common horizontal distance is 200 m. A is the bottom of the flagpole and B its top. Angle OPA is 34 degrees and angle OPB is 36 degrees, with a right angle at the building base O. Diagram coordinates derive both sight-line slopes from the given angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated heights or answer are included.

answer.worked:
Let $h_A$ and $h_B$ be the heights above ground of $A$ and $B$ respectively.

$$\begin{align*}\tan 34^{\circ} &= \frac{h_A}{200}\\h_A &= 200\tan 34^{\circ}\\\tan 36^{\circ} &= \frac{h_B}{200}\\h_B &= 200\tan 36^{\circ}\\AB &= h_B-h_A\\AB &= 200\tan 36^{\circ}-200\tan 34^{\circ}\\AB &\approx 10.4\ \mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$
